A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, Table 1, Figures 1–17, and Appendices A–M are available and can be matched despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original color-naming evaluations across 39 LLMs, iterated-learning simulations for colors and Shepard circles, and supplementary empirical analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental and simulation results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The IICLL procedure, constrained label selection, generation-to-generation sampling, and conversation-history mechanism are unchanged. Expanded descriptions do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions cover English color naming, WCS comparisons, artificial color-category transmission, and Shepard circles. The sRGB, CIELAB, and image-input scenarios already appear in v3.

E2.justification: The evaluated model roster and human comparisons are unchanged. The NN-rgb nearest-neighbor baseline highlighted in v4's main text already appears in v3 Appendix M and Figure 17. Removing WCS from Figure 11's caption corrects its description; the plotted comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The detailed experimental protocols retain the same models, stimuli, metrics, sampling, generation limits, and history windows. Section 4.3 newly specifies four allowed Shepard-circle labels for the existing experiment, without establishing a changed setting.

E4.justification: The CIELAB, multimodal-input, OLMo training-trajectory, rotation, history-window, smaller-model, and nearest-neighbor analyses already exist in v3. v4 expands their main-text discussion without adding or changing the supporting analyses.

E5.justification: The reporting of initializations, replications, and 95% confidence intervals is unchanged. Figure 11 retains the same normal-distribution assumption for its intervals; no new seed information or statistical procedure is supplied.

E6.justification: The result curves, numerical entries, trajectories, and category maps are unchanged across the matched figures and appendices. v4 makes existing comparisons, including Gemini versus human IL and NN-rgb, more explicit in prose.

T1.justification: Appendix A, Equation 2 corrects the mutual-information summation from m alone to m,w. Section 2.2 changes the stated parameter range from beta >= 1 to beta >= 0, although Appendix A, Equation 4 still specifies beta >= 1. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions and abstract claims remain intact. The introduction modestly broadens its concluding suggestion from IB-efficiency supporting intelligent behavior to 'optimal compression more generally.'

C2.justification: v4 interprets CIELAB failures as a difference between LLM and human color representations, qualifies rotation evidence for non-Gemini models as less conclusive, and explicitly leaves Shepard-circle IB-efficiency for future testing. It also attributes OLMo gains more strongly to instruction tuning, despite Appendix F retaining its description of pretraining on curated data.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement replaces a future code-release promise with a project code location and states that generated LLM data are available upon request. v4 also identifies the Shepard stimulus code and license and discloses the four-label Shepard setting. These are documented access and implementation details; external availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v4 adds Carr et al. (2020) as the source for Shepard stimulus generation and code, and removes the Bai et al. (2025) Qwen2.5-VL technical-report reference. The broader positioning relative to IB theory and iterated-learning research is unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 locally reorganizes and rewrites the results narrative, especially Section 4.1, bringing existing appendix findings into the main discussion. It also removes an introductory motivation paragraph, adjusts headings and terminology, and updates publication and acknowledgment text. The overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The figures and table retain their visual content. v4 adds publication headers, revises several captions, clarifies Figure 7's marker convention, and changes page flow. Appendix E's closing text spills onto an additional, mostly empty page.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's future code-release promise, v4 provides more concrete reproduction and data-access instructions and credits the Shepard code. The corrected mutual-information formula and clearer qualifications also provide modest benefits. These gains are tempered by the new main-text/appendix beta-range mismatch and the misleading OLMo training-stage description. The experimental evidence itself is unchanged.
